title.div: Housing affordability in Canada, 2024

summary.div: In 2024, 23.2% of Canadian households lived in housing unaffordable to them—defined as spending 30% or more of their income on shelter costs—up from 22.0% in 2022. Renters (33.7%) were more likely than owners (17.4%) to live in unaffordable housing. This gap has been stable since 2018, the first cycle of this survey.

title.div: Sector Based Producer Price Indexes: announcement

summary.div: Today, Statistics Canada announces the creation of the Sector Based Producer Price Indexes. These indexes have been built to measure price changes across four producer sectors—energy, non-energy, goods and services—using a methodology developed by the Bank of Canada. The indexes will be published for the first time on October 9, 2026. These data support research on firms' price-setting behaviours and inflation dynamics, including the development of economic models.

title.div: Health Reports, August 2026

summary.div: Environmental exposures such as air pollution, extreme heat and cold, and limited green space are known to affect health. When people move residences, their risk of exposure changes. Few national datasets have captured both exposures to multiple environments and residential mobility. The article entitled "Residential mobility and multi-domain environmental exposures in Canada: Development of the Residential Mobility Exposome File" introduces the Residential Mobility Exposome File (ReMEF) to fill this gap. The ReMEF linked residential historical postal codes to annual measures across three domains (ambient air pollution, built and green environment, and ambient temperature) using the Canadian Census Health and Environment Cohort for 1991, 1996 and 2001, with up to 25 years of follow-up.

title.div: Use of generative artificial intelligence tools among Canadian workers, March 2026

A new study release today, titled "The homeownership trajectories of recent immigrants," examines the relationship between immigration and housing by exploring the homeownership trajectories of recent immigrants in Prince Edward Island, Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Ontario, Manitoba, Alberta and British Columbia.

title.div: Study: Extreme weather impacts on consumers and insurers in Canada: An updated analysis, December 2019 to December 2025

summary.div: Canada's property and casualty (P&C) insurers have faced growing financial pressure, driven by an increase in extreme weather events, higher building and replacement costs, higher repair costs and a rise in vehicle prices and thefts. These factors have contributed to higher insurance expenses, and insurers have raised premiums to compensate. From December 2019 to December 2025, homeowners' home and mortgage insurance premiums increased 45.0%, more than double the increase in the all-item Consumer Price Index over this period (+21.0%). Passenger vehicle insurance premiums rose 23.9%, also outpacing overall inflation, albeit to a lesser degree.

title.div: Consumer Price Index: New basket weights, 2025

summary.div: Updated basket weights for the goods and services in the Consumer Price Index (CPI), representing consumer spending patterns in 2025, are now available. The 2025 basket will combine expenditure data from the Household Final Consumption Expenditures, the Survey of Household Spending and alternative data sources to account for shifts in spending.
